title: introduce-cost-thermostat-and-quant-steward-for-adaptive-batching
author: Owen Brooks
body:
Motivation: Production workloads show oscillating token-cost vs latency tradeoffs across tenants. Existing static defaults either waste GPU time or trigger unacceptable latency tails for some customers. This PR adds two coordinated components: (1) a lightweight runtime controller called the 'cost thermostat' that adjusts batching aggressiveness and cache TTLs per-tenant based on observed unit-econ signals and SLO pressure, and (2) a 'quant steward' policy that safely recommends and phases in quantization profiles while enforcing output-quality guardrails.

Summary of changes: Adds runtime controller, new CLI and rwctl surface, telemetry hooks, unit-econ scoring, and a safety policy engine to prevent blind quant rollouts. The thermostat uses an exponential moving average of tokens-per-second, tail-p95 latency deltas, and per-tenant cost targets to nudge batch sizes and cache TTLs. The quant steward manages staged rollouts by creating short-lived candidate variants and capturing a lightweight prompt-regression score; it will pause/rollback if score drift exceeds configured thresholds.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked (Linear ENG-1847) and high-level diagrams in docs/cost-thermostat.md.
- [x] End-to-end unit tests for thermostat and steward behaviors.
- [x] Metrics (econ.unit_cost, thermostat.setpoint, steward.rollback_count) wired into observability.
- [x] rwctl command for dry-run simulation and apply.
- [x] Safety: default conservative thresholds and opt-in tenant flag.

Related: Builds on runtime batching hooks introduced earlier but intentionally avoids changing kernel selection. Implements conservative defaults and an opt-in experiment flag for customers. See Linear ENG-1847 and ENG-2053 for the decision rationale.

Commit summary: see commits field for granular entries.

Changed areas (high level): pkg/econ/thermostat.go - controller and policy; pkg/quant/steward.go - staged rollout logic and telemetry; cmd/rwctl/cost_thermostat.go - CLI dry-run/apply commands; docs/cost-thermostat.md - operator guide and recommended defaults; observability/metrics/econ_metrics.yaml - new metric definitions and dashboards; tests/econ/thermostat_test.go and tests/quant/steward_test.go - unit and integration smoke tests.

CI notes: Unit tests failed initially on steward edge-case (null prompt bin), fixed in commit 3. All checks green on final run: unit, integration (smoke), lint, and telemetry smoke.

Review & merge: Addressed reviewer feedback to add stronger guardrails, rollback telemetry, and a rwctl dry-run mode. Squash-merged into main on 2024-11-18.

Operational notes: The controller is disabled by default; enable per-tenant via tenant config or global feature flag rw.feature.cost_thermostat=true. Rollouts should start in simulate mode (rwctl cost-thermostat --simulate).

review_comments: Priya Nair (2024-11-07): Question - how do we avoid oscillation when tenants have bursty traffic? Can thermostat add a cooldown or backoff?

Owen Brooks (2024-11-07): Reply - thermostat includes a configurable damping factor and exponential backoff (thermostat.cooldown_ms). Added tests demonstrating stability under synthetic burst patterns.
Lars Gunnarsson (2024-11-09): Request - quantify the rollback signal. Add a metric that captures 'steward.rollback_score' and emit the top-k prompts that triggered rollbacks for debugging.

Owen Brooks (2024-11-10): Done - steward now emits steward.rollback_score and a sampling of top rollback prompts to telemetry with PIIs stripped. Updated docs with instructions for using the prompt samples in evaluation harness.
Ethan Zhao (2024-11-12): Nit - CLI flags should be consistent with other rwctl subcommands (use dashed-names).
Owen Brooks (2024-11-12): Fixed - renamed flags to follow convention and added integration test for rwctl parsing.
ci_checks: integration-smoke: passed (runtime smoke on small cluster image)
telemetry-smoke: passed (metrics emitted and schemas validated)
security-scan: passed (no new dependencies pulled beyond allowed list)
release_notes: Add cost thermostat controller to adapt batching and cache TTLs per-tenant; introduce quant steward for safe, staged quantization rollouts. Disabled by default; enable via feature flag or tenant opt-in. Includes new observability metrics and rwctl commands for simulation and apply.
notes: This PR is intentionally conservative: controller defaults are designed to avoid automated aggressive quantization and require explicit opt-in for production tenants. Operators should monitor thermostat.setpoint and steward.rollback_count when enabling.
